report.headline: Projected usage climbs to 24.6% in the EuroLeague, well above the NBA usage rate of 19.5%, while the true-shooting projection carries no signal because the model loses to a trivial baseline on that metric.

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 24.6% in the EuroLeague, up from a 19.5% usage rate in the 2010-11 NBA season and above the EuroLeague's minutes-weighted average of 20.3%.

risks.text: The true-shooting projection is not usable: the model's out-of-fold error (4.5%) exceeds that of the trivial league-average baseline (4.3%), meaning the 54.2% figure carries no more information than simply assuming EuroLeague average shooting.

The 95% usage interval spans 17.9% to 31.3%, close to three EuroLeague standard deviations (4.4% each) wide, so while the group-level direction (higher usage) is credible, an individual projection cannot be pinned down.
This estimate rests on only 115 historical NBA-to-EuroLeague transitions, a relatively thin sample for projecting an individual case.

In the NBA season being used as the baseline, the subject's usage rate stood only 0.11 standard deviations above league average and true-shooting stood 0.52 standard deviations below it, and players who make this move already sit only 0.31 standard deviations above their league on average — a modest starting profile for projecting a larger EuroLeague role.

strengths.text: A heavy three-point diet in the NBA season, 44.0% of shot attempts, paired with a low turnover rate of 9.4%, suggests a low-risk offensive profile likely to persist as usage rises.
Assist rate of 13.1% (2.885 assists per 75 possessions) indicates some measure of shot creation beyond simple scoring, which supports the projected jump in usage.

The projected usage rate of 24.6% sits well above the 19.8% that simple standing-preservation (holding the same relative rank) would imply, and the fitted slope of 0.977 shows nearly all of the player's above-average NBA standing is expected to carry over to the EuroLeague.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage runs from 20.2% to 29.0%, and the 95% interval from 17.9% to 31.3% — a third of the EuroLeague's usage standard deviation of 4.4% on the tight side alone — so the model can say this is a heavier-role move but not pin the exact share; the true-shooting projection of 54.2% (80% interval 46.9%-61.6%, 95% interval 42.9%-65.5%) should not be trusted at all, since on held-out data the model's true-shooting error of 4.5% is worse than the 4.3% error of simply guessing the league average.
